attributes.title: Level 3

subgroups.name: build 1

steps.hints: ❓ Did you click on the ⏷in the red box to rename the sprite?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja:

❓ What would be a good name for your sprite that is simple and descriptive?


Sensei Pro Tip: 

💡Encourage the ninja to give sprites a simple yet descriptive name, as that will be helpful to refer to sprites clearly.
steps.instructions:
Put some food on the table!


Add a sprite to this project, and select the large ham image from the Gallery.


Rename the sprite with a simple, descriptive name such as “ham”. Click the ⏷ in the red [mySprite] name box to open the drop down menu, then select Rename variable…


Click ▶ to see the ham sprite appear on screen.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you select the correct sprite name in the [set sprite position to] block?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja: 

❓Which block sets a sprite’s position?

❓Did you try out different x and y values to move your sprite’s position?


Sensei Pro Tip: 

💡 Remind ninjas that any block that refers to a sprite needs to come after its [set sprite to] block.
steps.instructions:
Place the ham sprite on the table!


Set the ham sprite’s position, and be sure to click the ⏷ on the (mySprite) bubble to select the sprite’s name. Click in the white bubbles to change the x and y coordinate values so the ham sprite is in the middle of the table.


Click ▶ to see the position of the ham sprite.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you select the correct sprite name in the [set sprite to] and [set sprite position to] blocks?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja:

❓Which block sets a sprite?  

❓Which block sets a sprite’s position?

❓ Did you change the name from “mySprite” to something more descriptive?


Sensei Pro Tip: 

💡 Encourage the ninja to give sprites a simple yet descriptive name, as that will be helpful to refer to the sprite later on in the program.
steps.instructions:
Set a plate to put your ham on!


﻿Set and rename a sprite from the Gallery that is an image of a plate, then set the sprite’s position so the plate is in the center of the table. 


Click ▶ to see the position of the plate sprite.

steps.hints:
💡 Move multiple blocks by clicking on the top block in the stack, dragging it out, then dropping it into a new position.

﻿
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja:

❓Which block sets a sprite?  

❓Which block sets a sprite’s position?

❓ Did you change the name from “mySprite” to something more descriptive?


Sensei Pro Tip: 

💡 Encourage the ninja to give sprites a simple yet descriptive name, as that will be helpful to refer to the sprite later on in the program.
steps.instructions:
Oh no - the ham is under the plate! Change the sequence of the [set sprite to] blocks so the program creates the plate sprite first and the food sprite after. 


Drag the plate sprite’s [set sprite to] and [set sprite position to] blocks above the food sprite’s blocks. 


Click ▶ to see the food sprite appear on top of the plate sprite.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you select the fork sprite name in the [move sprite with buttons] and [set sprite stay in screen] blocks?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja:

❓ Did you drag the [move sprite with buttons] block inside the [on start] container block?

❓ Did you drag the [set sprite stay in screen]  block inside the [on start] container block?


Sensei Pro Tip: 

💡 Remind ninjas to select the correct sprite name in the new blocks.
steps.instructions:
Move the fork to eat dinner!


Open the Controller code block menu and drag a [move sprite with buttons] block underneath the fork sprite’s code blocks.


Then, open the Sprite code block menu and drag in a [set sprite stay in screen] block to keep the fork sprite from moving off the screen.


Click the ⏷ on both (mySprite) bubbles to select the fork sprite’s name.


Click ▶ then press the direction buttons to move the fork sprite around the screen and to the food on the plate!

steps.hints: 💡 Move multiple blocks by clicking on the top block in the stack that you want to move, dragging it out, then dropping it into a new position.
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja:

❓ Why does the fork sprite appear underneath the food sprite?

❓ Which code blocks should you move around to see the fork sprite in front of the plate and food sprite?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡The sequence of the code blocks matters. Sprites that are created first will appear behind other sprites.
steps.instructions:
Oh no - the fork is moving under the plate of food! Change the sequence of the [set sprite to] blocks so the program creates the fork sprite after the plate and food sprites. 


Drag the fork sprite’s blocks to a different location in the [on start] block.


Click ▶ to check your program until the fork sprite moves in front of the plate and food sprites.

steps.hints: ❓ Did you drag the [splash] block on top of the other blocks?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:


Ask the ninja:

❓ Did you drag the [splash] block inside the [on start] container block and place it at the top?


Sensei Pro Tip:

💡 Guide the ninja to notice that the sequence, or order, of the code blocks matters. Putting the blocks in a different order will change how the program runs.
steps.instructions:
Add directions to this project.


Open the Game code block menu and drag a [splash] block inside the [on start] container block on top of all the other blocks. Click the white bubble then type the game directions, such as “Move the fork to eat the ham.”  


Click ▶ to see the splash screen message appear at the start of this project.

steps.hints: ❓  Where should the [set background color]  block and  [play sound] block go?
steps.senseiHelp:
Solution:

﻿

Ask the ninja: ❓Where did you place the screen effect and play sound blocks? Do they work as you expected them to?

Sensei Pro Tip: 💡 Guide the ninja to notice that the sequence, or order, of the code blocks matters. Putting the blocks in a different order will change the order of how the program runs.

💡 Guide ninjas to note that while these customizing blocks are open ended and not required for the game to “work”, they really improve the Player’s experience playing a game, either by giving context to what the Player should do or not do, or to provide a more fun experience overall. They also allow the Ninja to add their personal touch and express themselves through small details present in the game.
steps.instructions:
Add some creative details to this project!


Open the Scene code block menu to drag a [set background color] block into this project, then open the Music code block menu to drag a [play sound] block into this project. Allow the sound to play [until done].


Click ▶ to see how these blocks changed this project!
